Failed to create database. Falling back to in-memory db: Error: unable to open database file
```

The shared Copilot state database is located under:

```

Therefore, this message does not look like simple SQLite corruption or a missing filesystem permission. title: Remote-SSH: file-path-declared activity bar icons missing (no icon, no tooltip) on 1.137.0 — regression of #11687 / #319834

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body:
### Summary
Activity bar icons for extensions running on the remote extension host are missing (no icon glyph, no hover tooltip) when connected via Remote-SSH, while the exact same window/session works fine locally (no SSH). The underlying view/panel is otherwise fully functional — only the Activity Bar icon contribution fails to render. This reproduces the symptom of microsoft/vscode-remote-release#11687 and microsoft/vscode#319834, which were closed as fixed in 1.124.0.

### Environment
- VS Code version: 1.137.0
- Local client: macOS
- Remote host: Ubuntu (Remote-SSH)
- Affected extensions:
  - `Anthropic.claude-code` 2.1.269
  - `ms-python.vscode-python-envs` 1.36.0

### Pattern observed
Both affected extensions declare their activity bar icon as a **file path to an SVG asset** (`resources/claude-logo.svg`, `files/logo.svg`). Extensions whose icons are **codicon font glyphs** instead (e.g. GitLens `$(gitlens-gitlens)`, GitHub Pull Requests `$(github)`) render correctly in the same window. This matches the previously identified root cause: file-based icon assets must be fetched from the remote host via `vscode-managed-remote-resource://`, which was reported to hit a CORS restriction; codicon glyphs are bundled locally and never need this fetch.

### Troubleshooting performed (ruling out state/cache corruption)
- Full reboot of the remote host (fresh boot id, fresh `vscode-server` process, fresh extension host) — no change
- Deleted the remote extension description cache (`CachedProfilesData/*/extensions.*.cache`) — no change
- Fully quit/relaunched the local client with `Cache`, `GPUCache`, `CachedData` cleared — no change
- Toggled the items via the Activity Bar's "Hidden Items" menu off/on — no change
- Removed the `when` conditions from the affected extension's `viewsContainers` as a test — no change
- Confirmed the extensions activate without error and their underlying views/panels work correctly when opened directly

### Workaround
Setting `"remote.SSH.useExecServer": false` immediately restores the missing icons, with no other extension breakage observed in this environment. This matches the workaround from #11687, suggesting this is the same underlying code path recurring rather than a new defect.

### Expected behavior
Activity bar icons declared via a file path should render identically over Remote-SSH as they do locally, without needing `remote.SSH.useExecServer` disabled.

### Additional context
Since #11687 / #319834 were closed as resolved in 1.124.0, and this reproduces on 1.137.0, this looks like either a regression or an incomplete fix of the original CORS/resource-loading issue.

title: Test: Connected document tabs and high-contrast document wells

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
Refs: #335605, #331104

- [ ] macOS
- [ ] windows
- [ ] linux

Complexity: 3

Authors: @chryw

---

The selected document tab now connects to the editor below it, while inactive tabs sit on the surrounding background. The goal is to make the active document easier to pick out without changing how you work with tabs.

Please explore the new appearance with your usual workflow and the settings below. Does anything look misaligned, become hard to read, or get in the way? Allow about 45-60 minutes; you don't need to try every combination.

## Set up

1. Use an Insiders build containing #335605. In the regular editor window, enable:

   ```json
   {
     "workbench.experimental.modernUI": true,
     "workbench.experimental.modernUIEditorTabStyle": "connected"
   }
   ```

2. Open a folder and several files: some short names, some long names, different extensions, and the same filename from two folders. Include a dotfile and a name with accented characters or emoji if convenient.
3. Leave one file unsaved, open one as a preview, and pin a few tabs using **Pin** in the tab context menu.

Screenshots and a short recording are in #335605.

## Things to try

- Select the first, middle, and last tabs, then hover their neighbors and Close buttons. The selected tab should join the document without a seam, the first tab should be flush with the left edge, and hover backgrounds should meet without gaps. Close icons should stay centered.
- Narrow and widen the window, resize the sidebar, and split the editor into groups. Try each tab sizing mode. Check that truncation, file extensions, icons, badges, and actions remain readable and don't overlap. Widening again should restore the labels and icons.
- Enable wrapping and get several rows. Select tabs on different rows. Bottom-row tabs connect to the document; upper rows use pills. Watch for uneven row heights, clipped corners, or a different background behind the Close button.
- Change pinned-tab sizes and put pinned tabs on a separate row. Reorder, pin/unpin, and close tabs while wrapped or scrolled. The selected tab and its actions should remain reachable.
- Try the default dark/light themes, Quiet Light, and both high-contrast themes. Switch between editor groups and another application. The active document should remain easy to identify. In high contrast, check the outline around the selected tab and document, including after the last tab closes.
- Navigate tabs and actions with the keyboard. Focus should remain visible, including at scroll edges. If you use a screen reader, check that truncated and icon-only tabs still have useful complete names and named actions.
- Switch to the `pill` style, turn Modern UI off, and try single/hidden tabs and Zen Mode. Check that their appearance restores cleanly. Theme-level color changes also affect classic tabs; connected corners should not.

## Tab appearance settings

Work through these settings with files already open. Try their available choices, then combine a few that put pressure on the layout: **left-side actions + narrow tabs**, **compact height + wrapped rows**, and **icons off + compact pins**.

Unless a full name is shown, settings below start with **`workbench.editor.`**.

| Area | Settings and choices |
| --- | --- |
| Style | `workbench.experimental.modernUI`: on/off; `workbench.experimental.modernUIEditorTabStyle`: `connected` / `pill` |
| Visible tabs | `showTabs`: `multiple` / `single` / `none` |
| Density | `window.density.editorTabHeight` and `window.density.layout`: `default` / `compact` |
| Sizing | `tabSizing`: `fit` / `shrink` / `fixed`; `wrapTabs`: on/off |
| Fixed widths | `tabSizingFixedMinWidth`, `tabSizingFixedMaxWidth`: default **50/160**, a smaller **38/38**, and a larger **100/240** range. These settings apply to `fixed`, not `fit` or `shrink`. |
| Pinned tabs | `pinnedTabSizing`: `normal` / `compact` / `shrink`; `pinnedTabsOnSeparateRow`: on/off |
| Tab actions | `tabActionLocation`: `left` / `right`; `tabActionReserveSpace`, `tabActionCloseVisibility`, `tabActionUnpinVisibility`: each on/off. Include dirty and pinned tabs. |
| Editor toolbar | `editorActionsLocation`: `default` / `titleBar` / `hidden`; `alwaysShowEditorActions`: on/off. Compare active/inactive and locked/unlocked groups. |
| Icons | `showIcons`: on/off; `workbench.iconTheme`: None / Seti / Minimal. If you have another `workbench.productIconTheme` installed, check action icons with it too. |
| Names and paths | `labelFormat`: `default` / `short` / `medium` / `long`; `showTabIndex`: on/off, including more than nine tabs |
| Custom names | `customLabels.enabled`: on/off; `customLabels.patterns`: try `"**/*.ts": "${filename} - ${dirname}"`, then a label with literal dotted text. Check truncation and hover text. |
| Untitled editors | `untitled.labelFormat`: `content` / `name`, with a long first line |
| Decorations | `decorations.badges`, `decorations.colors`, `highlightModifiedTabs`: each on/off, with unsaved files and Git/problem decorations |
| Preview tabs | `enablePreview`, `enablePreviewFromQuickOpen`, `enablePreviewFromCodeNavigation`: on/off. Open files through the corresponding route and check italic names/extensions. |
| Scrollbars | `titleScrollbarSizing`: `default` / `large`; `titleScrollbarVisibility`: `auto` / `visible` / `hidden`, with overflowing tabs |
| Colors | `workbench.colorTheme`; `workbench.colorCustomizations`: try explicit tab foreground/hover colors and a translucent `editorGroupHeader.tabsBackground`. Check for mismatched hover patches or darker overlaps. |

Also check the surrounding header with `breadcrumbs.enabled` on/off, `zenMode.showTabs` set to each tab mode, and a different `window.zoomLevel`. With editor actions in the title bar, try the supported `window.titleBarStyle` / `window.customTitleBarVisibility` choices. If you follow the system appearance automatically, switch it while tabs are wrapped or compressed.

When filing a bug, include your tab settings, theme, and a screenshot or short recording. Feedback on readability and whether the active document stands out is welcome too.

title: Webview can go blank when an earlier mount finishes after a remount
body:
I’m seeing intermittent blank MCP App views in the main Chat panel on Windows, with VS Code 1.135.0 (`08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5`). The tool calls and resource reads succeed, but some views never get an inner iframe. Reload Window restores them.

I found a race in `WebviewElement.mountTo` that reproduces the blank view:

1. Start a mount and leave its `parentOriginHash` promise pending.
2. Remount the same webview and let the second hash finish.
3. Let the first hash finish after the second view has connected.

The first completion still calls `_initElement`, resetting the iframe. The webview retains a message port, but the replacement frame stays blank.

I tested this in an isolated VS Code window by delaying the first hash result by 350ms. Ignoring a hash completion when its promise is no longer the current mount promise kept all three test views visible across three repeated rounds. The encoded origin needs the same check, so an older completion cannot overwrite it either.

[Small source patch and standalone regression check](https://github.com/absolutejs/mcp/tree/2c4bb1f/canary/vscode). The check executes `mountTo` extracted from the upstream TypeScript file: both obsolete-completion cases fail before the patch and pass afterward. It is not the full VS Code test suite. The same mount method is present on current main.

This may be related to #331140, but I reproduced this in the main Chat panel, without an auxiliary window. I haven’t established that this race explains every blank MCP App report.

Three `CopilotAgent` tests fail on a clean checkout when `COPILOT_HOME` is set:

title: Show all accounts used by AI providers and MCP servers in the profile menu
body:
## Problem

The Copilot profile menu currently shows the GitHub account and ChatGPT sign-in, but it does not provide a way to see the other accounts used by AI-related features. The existing Accounts menu can show some of these accounts, but that leaves the Copilot profile menu incomplete and makes it difficult to understand which identities are active for AI features.

This matters because:

- MCP servers can depend on authenticated accounts.
- BYOK providers such as Azure AI Foundry depend on accounts.
- Microsoft sign-in for inference will add another account-backed flow.

## Expected

Provide a coherent account story in the Copilot profile menu that displays all accounts currently used by AI providers, MCP servers, and inference, with a path to inspect or manage them. The UI should scale beyond GitHub and ChatGPT rather than adding one-off entries for each provider.

The existing Accounts menu may be useful prior art, though its current presentation should not necessarily be copied as-is.

Add a default-off local canvas development preview to the Agents Window, backed by approved Copilot SDK extension packages and source-resolved native browser surfaces.

- Focused unit/integration coverage and isolated developer launch/runbook support.

The five JavaScript allowlist additions are executable extension/browser fixtures and the no-build authoring starter; those files intentionally run as delivered rather than requiring TypeScript transpilation. The allowlist still requires normal CODEOWNERS review.

title: Sessions list can show stale In Progress status when input is needed
body:
## Repro / user impact

1. Start an Agent Host session that has multiple chats, such as a main chat and a tool-created subagent chat.
2. Leave the session open long enough for the provider's 30-second full session-state subscription lease to expire, or switch away so that the session is no longer visible.
3. Let the main chat reach a point where it asks the user for input.
4. Observe the session in the Sessions list.
5. Click the session to open it.

**Actual:** Before opening the session, its list row can continue to show **In Progress** even though the session is waiting for input. Opening it immediately changes the row to **Input Needed**.

**Expected:** The Sessions list should change to **Input Needed** as soon as the main chat requests input, without requiring the user to open the session.

This makes sessions that require attention look as if they are still doing background work, so users can miss or delay required input.

## Confirmed behavior

An Agent Host debug trace captured the following sequence:

- The main chat started an `ask_user` tool call.
- The host emitted `session/chatUpdated` with `InputNeeded`.
- The host emitted `root/sessionSummaryChanged` with `InputNeeded | IsRead`.
- Later `listSessions` responses also returned `InputNeeded | IsRead`.
- The Sessions list continued to show the stale state until the session was opened.

This confirms that the Agent Host's session summary is current; the stale state is in the VS Code-side presentation path.

## Root cause

The primary Sessions list intentionally derives the parent row from the main chat rather than the aggregate `session.status`. It also shows `InProgress` when any chat is active:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts#L224-L234

For multi-chat Agent Host sessions, `mainChat.status` comes from a separate default-chat status override populated by the full `SessionState` chat catalog:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L1289-L1294

The provider releases that full session-state subscription after 30 seconds when it is no longer pinned by a visible session:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L5392

After the lease expires, `root/sessionSummaryChanged` correctly updates the aggregate `session.status`, but it does not update the cached default-chat status. The list continues reading the stale `mainChat.status`. Opening the session re-establishes the full-state subscription and applies the current chat catalog, which makes the row update.

There is already a provider test that demonstrates the underlying stale-cache behavior after the subscription expires:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts#L6573

## Fix considerations

Copying the aggregate status into `mainChat.status` is not generally correct: a peer chat can promote the aggregate session to `InputNeeded`, while the parent row is intentionally supposed to reflect the main chat. A complete fix likely needs either:

- enough default-chat/active-chat information in the lightweight session summary and its deltas; or
- a different subscription strategy that keeps the status inputs used by visible list rows current.

The relevant parent-row behavior was introduced in #332931 and extended in #333999.

title: MCP migration blocks same-name servers in different workspace roots
body:
- MCP migration rejects same-name servers across workspace roots, even though each server would move into its own root’s `.mcp.json` without overwriting the other.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a trusted multi-root workspace containing `root-a` and `root-b`.
2. Create `.vscode/mcp.json` in each root with identical contents:
   ```json
   {
     "servers": {
       "same": {
         "type": "stdio",
         "command": "npx",
         "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```
   Leave both workspace-root `.mcp.json` files absent.
3. Set `chat.customizations.mcpServerMigration.enabled` to `true`, `chat.mcp.access` to `"all"`, and `chat.mcp.autostart` to `"never"`. Starting the servers is unnecessary.
4. Select an Agent Host / Copilot CLI session whose scope includes both roots.
5. Open **Chat: Open Customizations → Migrations → Migrate MCP Servers**, select an offered `same` entry, and confirm migration.

- **Expected:** Each entry can migrate to its own root’s `.mcp.json`. A matching name in another root should not, by itself, block independent file migration.
- **Actual, confirmed in code and existing tests:** Migration rejects the entry because another workspace root defines the same name and asks the user to rename or remove the duplicate.
- **Extensions disabled:** Not checked.

<details>
<summary>Details for investigation</summary>

- Found while investigating #335820. The refresh-loop fix in #335860 does not change this restriction.
- The [migration guard](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/658f8e95803a59b458bbd8ca0c11124564dbded5/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/mcpServerCustomizationMigration.ts#L253-L287) treats a matching name in another root’s source or destination as a conflict, regardless of whether the configurations are identical.
- There is a separate runtime consideration: [session MCP discovery](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/658f8e95803a59b458bbd8ca0c11124564dbded5/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/sessionMcpDiscovery.ts#L178-L190) merges roots by server name, with the first root winning. Per-root default working directories can also differ. Allowing migration must account for runtime precedence rather than silently changing which server is used.
- The cross-root rejection was verified from source and existing migration tests; the manual UI sequence above was not executed during this investigation.

</details>

title: mcp: stabilize discovery and coalesce migration refreshes
body:
## Summary

- Stop migration-panel refresh loops when multiple workspace roots define the same MCP server names.
- Collapse duplicate MCP notifications and migration refresh bursts instead of repeating discovery for every event.
- Cancel obsolete migration discovery when a newer refresh supersedes it or the editor closes, while preserving genuine updates and error reporting.

Fixes #335820

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Installed MCP discovery selected duplicate-name winners from the runtime-dependent display order. Publishing a winner moved it ahead of the other root's entry, which made the other entry win the next discovery pass. Replacing the runtime servers repeated this cycle.

Overlapping workbench subscriptions amplified each replacement into multiple notifications. The migration editor also observed several related inputs and started a computation for each notification. Its sequence guard discarded stale results only after the work had already happened.

### Implementation

- Discovery sorts a copy of the installed inventory by name and ID before applying existing scope precedence. Display ordering remains independent of discovery selection.
- One workbench observer handles runtime inventory and per-server enablement changes, re-sorts the display inventory, and emits the change notification.
- A zero-delay delayer coalesces migration refresh requests within a burst. The generation advances when a refresh is requested, immediately invalidating older work rather than waiting for the replacement computation to start.
- Each active refresh owns a cancellation token. It reaches file and MCP migration computation, destination-folder discovery, and MCP source-file reads. Cancelled planning stops before reading additional roots.
- Closing, recreating, or disposing the editor cancels pending work; reopening requests fresh migration information. Generation, session, harness, and cancellation checks prevent late results from being applied, including results from providers that do not cooperate with cancellation.

### Behavior and constraints

- Real configuration, enablement, and policy changes still trigger refreshes. This does not disable discovery or cache migration results indefinitely.

labels.name: terminal-shell-integration
labels.description: Shell integration infrastructure, command decorations, etc.

body:
Shell integration tracks the terminal's current working directory from OSC 633 property reports. Process-terminal reports currently update the recorded CWD even when the shell integration nonce is missing or does not match.

Since terminal output can contain arbitrary OSC sequences, an unverified report can replace the terminal's CWD state and affect features that rely on it.

The fix should:

- Include the terminal nonce in built-in shell and task CWD reports.
- Ignore process-terminal CWD reports without an exact, non-empty nonce match.
- Preserve nonce-less CWD reports from extension-owned and custom pseudoterminals as untrusted.
- Keep that compatibility behavior correct when terminals are reused, recorded and replayed by the PTY host, transported to a remote extension host, or restored from persistent panel/editor state.
- Re-publish only extension ownership before persistent replay rather than overwriting the restored launch configuration.
- Preserve the last accepted CWD after an invalid report.
- Keep Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, and task terminal behavior aligned.

Compatibility notes:

- The nonce is intentionally removed from the environment after the initial integration starts. Manually integrated nested or relayed process shells cannot inherit it, so their nonce-less CWD reports are ignored and CWD-dependent features may retain the parent CWD until a trusted report resumes.
- PowerShell emits the CWD nonce as prompt output, matching the existing nonce-bearing `EnvJson` report. Visible prompt rendering on Windows 10 still requires manual verification before merge.
- Older remote or serialized processes that do not provide extension ownership remain strict for that restoration rather than guessing that the terminal is extension-owned.

This issue is scoped to OSC 633 CWD property handling. Other CWD-reporting protocols and Agent Host terminal CWD policy are unchanged.

title: Allow line numbers to be rendered on the right side of the editor
body:
<!-- ⚠️️ For bug reports, please search existing issues first. This is a feature request. -->

### Problem

Line numbers are rendered exclusively in the left gutter, and there is no way to move them. For some workflows the left gutter is the wrong place for them:

- Code is left-aligned, so the eye is already anchored on the left edge. Numbers sitting between the window edge and the code push the code right and add a column of visual noise directly adjacent to the text you are reading.
- When referencing line numbers while reading toward the end of a line (long lines, wrapped prose, log files, minified or generated output), the number is at the opposite side of the screen from where you are looking.
- With line numbers off, the left edge is clean but the numbers are gone entirely — there is no middle ground.

### Why existing options do not solve this

`editor.lineNumbers` only accepts `on` / `off` / `relative` / `interval` — all of which render in the left gutter. `editor.glyphMargin`, `editor.folding`, and `editor.lineDecorationsWidth` change the gutter's contents and width but not its side.

Extensions cannot solve it either. The extension API only exposes gutter decorations (`gutterIconPath`) and `before`/`after` inline decorations. The "Double Line Numbers" extension (https://github.com/slhsxcmy/vscode-double-line-numbers) is the closest attempt — it renders a second set of numbers as SVG gutter icons — but both sets still live in the left gutter, and using it means giving up breakpoint glyphs. Inline `after` decorations cannot produce a stable right-aligned column because they follow the end of each line's text rather than a fixed column.

So this needs core support.

### Proposed solution

A setting controlling which side the line number column renders on, e.g.:

```jsonc
"editor.lineNumbersPosition": "left" | "right"  // default: "left"
```

`"right"` would render the line number column against the right edge of the editor's content area (inside the vertical scrollbar and minimap), with the existing `editor.lineNumbers` modes (`on`/`relative`/`interval`) and `editor.lineNumbersMinChars` continuing to apply. The left gutter would keep the glyph margin, folding controls, and SCM decorations, so breakpoints and diff markers are unaffected.

Open questions worth deciding: interaction with the minimap and `editor.minimap.side`, and whether click-to-select-line on the numbers should move with them (it should).

### Real-world scenarios

- Reading long-line content (logs, generated code, CSVs, wrapped Markdown) where the relevant line number should be near the end of the line, not the start.
- Pairing / screen sharing where someone calls out a line number: with the numbers adjacent to the right edge, the number and the scrollbar position agree.
- Minimal editing setups that want the code flush against the left edge without losing line numbers entirely.
- Users coming from editors and terminal tools that allow right-side or configurable gutters.

### Prior art / related issues

Related gutter-configuration requests, none of which cover position: #91067 (gutter border), #30795 (gutter width), #135114 (content left padding), #13212 (hide gutter).

title: Validate OSC 633 CWD reports with shell integration nonces
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335858

- Require process-terminal OSC 633 CWD updates to carry the terminal's exact, non-empty shell integration nonce; ignore missing, empty, or mismatched reports while preserving the prior CWD.
- Keep nonce-less CWD reports working for extension-owned and custom pseudoterminals, while marking those updates as untrusted.
- Keep nonce-less reports from manually integrated nested or relayed process shells rejected because the nonce is intentionally removed from the environment; those shells may retain the parent CWD until a trusted report resumes.
- Update the compatibility policy when a terminal is reused, so process and custom-PTY tasks cannot inherit each other's behavior.
- Carry extension ownership through remote launch transport and persistent process details.
- Apply the same compatibility policy in the PTY-host recorder so completed and partial command CWD metadata survives replay.
- Restore extension ownership through an ownership-only process property before persistent replay, without overwriting the restored executable, arguments, environment, or CWD.
- Append the same nonce to serialized CWD reports from Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, and task startup.
- Keep the Fish nonce in global shell scope so prompt hooks can include it after initialization.
- Emit the PowerShell CWD nonce as prompt output, matching the existing nonce-bearing `EnvJson` report; Windows 10 prompt rendering still requires manual verification.
- Rewrite task `initialText` to the live or persisted terminal nonce during reuse and reconnection for both string and object forms.
- Keep Agent Host property parsing compatible with the optional nonce without including it in the decoded CWD or changing terminal-management policy.
- Keep OSC 7, OSC 9;9, OSC 1337, and Agent Host CWD trust policy unchanged; this PR is scoped to Workbench OSC 633 handling.

## Testing

- Passed 57 targeted Node tests with 9 expected platform skips, covering PTY-host recorder metadata, reattach/revive ordering, remote server transport, Agent Host parser compatibility, and shell emitters.
- Passed 188 targeted Electron tests with 2 existing pending cases, covering strict process-terminal validation, live reuse transitions, remote client transport, persistent extension-terminal reconstruction, old editor-state hydration, serialized delimiters, task startup, and reused-terminal nonce rewriting.
- Passed Bash, Zsh, and Fish syntax and runtime checks.
- Passed `transpile-client`, targeted ESLint, full repository hygiene, and diff checks.
- PowerShell runtime was unavailable on macOS. Its source emission is covered by the terminal environment test suite, but visible prompt rendering on Windows 10 has not been manually verified.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- OSC 633 CWD argument framing comes from [`ShellIntegrationAddon` property handling](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/xterm/shellIntegrationAddon.ts#L571-L590); this keeps the serialized property in the first argument and the terminal nonce in the second.
- Separate nonce framing follows the existing shell command reports in [Bash](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration-bash.sh#L350-L356), [Zsh](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration-rc.zsh#L256-L260), [Fish](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.fish#L104-L119), and [PowerShell](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.ps1#L134-L145).
- Task CWD serialization and nonce placement follow [`taskShellIntegrationStartSequence`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/browser/terminalTaskSystem.ts#L182-L201).
- Reconnection handling builds on the existing task-terminal reuse flow in [`terminalTaskSystem.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/browser/terminalTaskSystem.ts#L1592-L1603).

### Type of issue

Bug

### Description

When asking Copilot in a normal VS Code window to create worktrees and do work in them, the newly created sessions are assigned to **Local** rather than the current workspace when using voice mode. They do not appear to retain awareness of the workspace, and after creation the session can disappear from the expected session list.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a workspace in the normal VS Code window.
2. Ask Copilot to create one or more worktrees and perform work in them using voice mode
3. Observe the newly created agent sessions.

### Expected behavior

The sessions remain associated with the originating workspace/worktrees and remain visible in the expected session list.

### Actual behavior

The sessions are created under **Local**, appear not to know about the originating workspace, and can vanish after creation. Instead, the sessions should use whatever harness is selected or default to **Copilot**.
